<description>
`CService::GetKey()` didn't include the network in the output. So in theory it would be possible for two IP2 and Tor addresses to have the same output from `CService::GetKey()`.

This would have unexpected results when used in the per-peer bloom filter of known addresses - we may wrongfully assume that a peer knows `foo.onion` when we have sent to them `foo.i2p`.

To make this impossible - include the network in `CService::GetKey()`.

Addrman already includes the network separately so it does not need this change. The code would be simplest if addrman also uses `GetKey()` with the network but that would mess the positions of addresses in existent databases (`peers.dat`). So, keep a variant of network-less `GetKey()` for addrman.

Thanks, @l0rinc for pointing me into this. I think it is minor but also the change is minor, so worth fixing IMO.
</description>
